title: Schema compliance enforcer and progressive ingestion fallback
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Introduce a tolerant-first schema compliance enforcer for usage events that progressively tightens validation and routes malformed or legacy payloads to a normalized fallback path. Goal: reduce customer-facing ingest errors, improve downstream analytics quality, and enable safe rollouts of stricter schema rules without data loss.
context: Current ingestion pipeline rejects a small but recurring set of usage events due to evolving client payload shapes. Rejection spikes correlate with SDK upgrades and partial-rollouts. We need a system that enforces a contract for new fields while preserving older/unknown properties for later reconciliation and analytics, plus clear observability for debugging.
acceptance_criteria: New schema enforcer accepts valid events and rejects only truly malformed events (invalid JSON, missing routing fields)
Malformed-but-recoverable events are archived to a fallback normalizer queue and marked with provenance metadata
Pipeline emits metrics for rejection rate, normalization rate, and per-field transformation counts
Canary rollout toggles allow enabling strict mode for a percentage of traffic and automatic rollback on regression
No increase in 95th-percentile ingestion latency above 12ms on p95 for the primary flow
implementation_notes: Design two logical stages: (1) fast surface-level validation for routing and required identifiers, implemented as an async prefilter in the ingestion gateway; (2) an adaptive field-level validator/normalizer in the ingestion workers that can apply transformation rules (type coercions, field renames, defaulting) and emit transformation diffs. Use protobuf/opentelemetry attributes for provenance. Persist original payload to an append-only raw store for 30d for replay.
architecture_decisions: Keep gateway prefilter CPU-light; only JSON parse + required keys check to avoid adding latency
Worker validators run in a separate consumer group so fallback normalization can be retried independently
Transformation rules are stored in a small feature table (S3 + versioned manifest) so we can evolve without code deploys
Fallback path writes normalized event and an "original_replay_key" pointer to raw store to support downstream reprocessing
tradeoffs: Pros: preserves data, reduces customer-visible errors, enables gradual tightening
Cons: additional storage costs for raw payloads, more complex replay tooling, slight increase to end-to-end processing time for fallback items
telemetry_and_alerting: Emit Prometheus metrics: ingest_prefilter_total, ingest_prefilter_rejects, normalize_queue_depth, normalize_success, normalize_failures, transform_field_{fieldname}_count. Create Grafana dashboard and alerts: reject_rate > 0.5% sustained for 10m, normalize_failures > 1% and normalize_queue_depth > 5000. Capture a 1% sample of transformed events for retention in BigQuery for debugging.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature-flag deploy in dev and staging; 2) Canary at 1% traffic for 24h with synthetic load and sample inspection; 3) Ramp to 10% for 48h; 4) Monitor metrics and error dashboards; 5) Gradual ramp to 100% if no regressions. During ramp, automatic rollback triggers on reject_rate or p95 latency regressions.
qa_steps: Unit tests for transformation rules and schema manifests
Integration tests: send legacy payloads, malformed payloads, and new-schema payloads; verify routes and normalized output
Load test gateway prefilter to validate p95 latency under production-like traffic
End-to-end test that reprocessing from raw store yields equivalent analytics aggregates
security_considerations: Sensitive fields must be redacted in the raw store. Normalizer must apply KMS encryption for raw payloads at rest and use ephemeral keys for transform logs. Audit events must be emitted for schema changes.
open_questions: How long do we retain original payloads for compliance and replay? (proposal: 30d, revisit with legal)
Should transformation manifests support conditional transforms based on customer plan or region?
Owner for transformation rule governance and rollback process?
